additions.reason: The brain (מֹחַ) is explicitly called a bechina of the wick (פְּתִילָה) in the candle metaphor central to Torah 225: 'וְהַמֹּחַ הִיא הַפְּתִילָה.' The brain is the wick of the candle whose oil is the moisture (= שמן in Package 1) and whose flame is the soul/light. This is a direct bechina-identification in the source text. As the structural center of the intellect-candle metaphor it belongs in Package 1 alongside לחלוחית/שמן and קיום השכל/נר דולק.

The wick (פְּתִילָה) is identified as a bechina of the brain (מֹחַ): 'וְהַמֹּחַ הִיא הַפְּתִילָה.' As the wick that the oil-moisture feeds and the soul-flame burns on, the wick/brain is a core element of the candle metaphor for the intellect. It belongs in Package 1 as another facet of the sustained-sekhel/burning-candle domain.

The soul within the brain is explicitly identified as the light/flame (אוֹר) in the candle metaphor: 'וְהַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמֹּחַ הוּא הָאוֹר.' This is a direct bechina-equation. The soul-in-the-brain and the candle's flame are two expressions of the same reality: the active, luminous life-force of the intellect. It belongs in Package 1.

The light/flame (אוֹר) is the bechina of the soul within the brain ('הַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמֹּחַ הוּא הָאוֹר'). As the luminous output of the intellect-candle metaphor, the light belongs in Package 1 alongside the candle (נר דולק) and its fuel (שמן/לחלוחית). The light IS the soul's active presence in the sekhel, not a product separate from it.

The Cherubim spreading their wings over the ark-cover are identified via the Zohar as a bechina of 'כַּפֻּרְתָּא דְּלִבָּא' — the lungs' wings sheltering the heart: 'וְזֶה בְּחִינַת וְהָיוּ הַכְּרוּבִים פּוֹרְשֵׂי כְנָפַיִם עַל הַכַּפֹּרֶת – כַּפֻּרְתָּא דְּלִבָּא.' The wings of the lungs (רֵאָה) and the wings of the Cherubim share the same essential nature: the protective coolness that shields the heart-fire and enables the brain's moisture. This bechina belongs in Package 1 as a description of the physiological mechanism underlying the sekhel-candle system.

additions.reason: The mouth (פֶּה) is identified as a bechina of speech (דִּבּוּר) via the verse-interpretation 'בְּפִיךָ – זוֹ צְדָקָה' and the proof 'מִי שָׂם פֶּה לָאָדָם.' The text states explicitly: 'עַל יְדֵי צְדָקָה נַעֲשֶׂה הַפֶּה, דְּהַיְנוּ הַדִּבּוּר.' The mouth and speech are the same entity (the mouth IS the speech-faculty of man), belonging with Package 2 which is defined by the אדם = דבור bechina. The missing direct bechina edge is פֶּה ↔ דִּבּוּר (or פֶּה ↔ אָדָם).
additions.source_quote: עַל יְדֵי צְדָקָה נַעֲשֶׂה הַפֶּה, דְּהַיְנוּ הַדִּבּוּר, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת גֶּדֶר הָאָדָם

additions.reason: The 'definition/category of man' (גֶּדֶר אָדָם) is the very content of Package 2: the Rebbe states that man is defined by his faculty of speech ('גֶּדֶר הָאָדָם שֶׁהוּא מְדַבֵּר'). גֶּדֶר אָדָם and דִּבּוּר are bechinas of each other — both are the definition of humanity as speech-being. This bechina edge (גֶּדֶר אָדָם ↔ דִּבּוּר / אָדָם) is missing from the dataset; currently גדר אדם appears only as a node2 in an eitza edge (ref=225, edge 614).
additions.source_quote: כִּי עִקַּר הַהֶבְדֵּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בֵּין אָדָם לְחַי הוּא עַל יְדֵי חִתּוּךְ הַדִּבּוּר, שֶׁהוּא גֶּדֶר הָאָדָם שֶׁהוּא מְדַבֵּר
